problems.title: Invalid answers change the refusal-rate denominator
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v5 Section 2, PDF p.4; Section 3.5, PDF pp.8–9; src/eval.py, easy_eval and process_layer_evaluation
claim: Section 2 describes refusal over all test examples. `src/eval.py`, `easy_eval` and `process_layer_evaluation`, instead discard invalid inversion labels before computing the saved rate.
analysis: For replies No, Certainly and two abstentions, one negative answer among all four is \(1/4\), but the conditional valid-only rate is \(1/2\). The substring branches also accept “unknown” as containing “no” while rejecting uppercase “NO”. These are denominator and parser differences, not estimates of the actual frequency in Figure 4.
result: The released rate is conditional on accepted labels. The original prediction counts are needed to determine the numerical impact.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Retain negative, affirmative and invalid counts. Report unconditional rate \(N_{\rm No}/N\), validity, and any separately named valid-only rate. Use an explicit case-insensitive label contract rather than unrestricted substrings.
problems.impact_rationale: A release evaluation convention differs from the paper; the published effect size is not corrected.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Direction extraction defaults to the wrong model template
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v5 Section 2, PDF p.3, model-template convention; src/extract_hidden.py, generate_directions; src/utils.py, formatInp_llama_persuasion
claim: The advertised Qwen/Llama3 extraction path calls the prompt formatter without its model argument; `src/utils.py` defaults that argument to Llama2. Intervention passes the model explicitly.
analysis: Thus the same selected model can receive Llama2 markers during extraction and model-specific markers during intervention. This changes the formatted sequence and semantic token positions. The release does not establish the extraction provenance of every cached direction.
result: The public reproduction path has a template mismatch; cached directions and cross-model results remain unverified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Pass the selected model explicitly, use the same template as intervention, and identify instruction positions on the complete tokenized sequence rather than an unverified isolated-suffix length.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a reproducibility path discrepancy with unresolved historical impact.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Direction and intervention support vary together
problems.source_location: Current arXiv v5 Section 3.5, PDF pp.8–9; Appendix E.1, PDF p.20, Figure 10
claim: Section 3.5 compares harmfulness and refusal interventions; Appendix E.1 explicitly discloses their different token masks.
analysis: Writing outcomes as \(Y(v,m)\), comparing \(Y(v_h,m_{\rm inst})\) with \(Y(v_r,m_{\rm all})\) changes both direction and support. It identifies different intervention packages, rather than an isolated direction effect. Appendix E.1 explicitly explains this choice, and Figure 10 retains the same-support refusal controls.
result: This disclosed design choice does not establish a separate error or invalidate all evidence for distinct directions.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a scope clarification with disclosed controls, not a newly supported defect.
problems.existing_correction_status: Scope clarification only; no author-paper repair or adoption is asserted.
